description: Extracts the time-changing spectral contour (formant trajectory) of the sound and replaces the signal underneath it with an endlessly rising or falling Shepard tone. Pinned to submode 1 (Shepard tones); submodes 2 (inharmonic glide, adds an hzstep parameter) and 3 (self-glissando) are separate entries if curated later. Exactly one of the two formant-extraction flags (-f or -p) is required. Operates on PVOC analysis files (.ana).
musical_use: The original sound is replaced by an endlessly glissandoing tone, but its articulations survive — rhythm, attack transients and speech-like patterning of the spectral envelope remain recognisably the same while the tone itself is transformed. glisrate is the key parameter: a low value such as 0.3 gives a twangy, vibrating sound; high values (around +/-50) push noise into the result. Positive glisses rise forever, negative fall. Because formants drive the process, sources with strong resonance features work best — voice, and lower drums especially (one trial turned a low drum into something not unlike a didgeridoo). The band-count (-f/-p) mostly affects analysis resolution rather than the character of the effect, while lowering topfrq offers a degree of filtering control.

fchans.description: Extract the formant envelope linear frequency-wise, using 1 point for every N equally-spaced frequency channels. Mutually exclusive with pbands — supply exactly one of the two. Scalar only (a breakpoint file is refused: 'Cannot read count of formant_bands.').

pbands.description: Extract the formant envelope linear pitchwise, using N equally-spaced pitch-bands per octave. Mutually exclusive with fchans — supply exactly one of the two. afta8/SoundThread suggest 1-12 (SoundThread default 8), but CDP accepts 0 without complaint. Scalar only (a breakpoint file is refused).

glisrate.description: Rate of glissing in semitones per second; negative values gliss downward. Low values (~0.3) are twangy and vibrating, high magnitudes (~50) noisy. SoundThread's musical slider spans -20 to 20 (default 1); afta8 allows -100 to 100. May vary over time via a breakpoint file (verified).

topfrq.description: Top of the spectrum; must exceed 2x the analysis channel width (~86 Hz for a 1024-point analysis at 44.1 kHz). Default: Nyquist. Lowering it acts as a crude filter. Scalar only — a breakpoint file is refused ('brkpnt_files not permitted').

examples.description: Slow rising Shepard tone under the source's formant contour, 8 pitch-bands per octave.
examples.expected_use: Replace a vocal or drum sound's tone with an ever-rising gliss while keeping its rhythm and articulation.

examples.description: Fast falling gliss with a capped spectrum.
examples.expected_use: Darker, band-limited falling Shepard texture from the same articulations.

known_issues: Exactly one of fchans (-f) or pbands (-p) must be supplied: with neither, CDP refuses with 'Formant parameter missing on cmdline.' (exit 255); with both, the second flag is mis-parsed as the glisrate positional and the run fails ('ERROR: Cannot read parameter 1 [-p8]').
pbands=0 is accepted with exit 0 despite afta8/SoundThread floors of 1 — the banner's 'N equally-spaced pitch-bands' is not range-enforced on this build.
The banner's 'default: nyquist' for topfrq is trusted from the banner/manual; afta8's def of 1000 Hz is a UI seed value, not the CDP default.
